comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh 31 October2026 public OSIRIS examination programme ECONOMIE/FEWBA26EC controls the2026 entrant pathway:60+60+60EC. The selected broad-identity major has compulsory Economics of Markets and Organisations4 and Impact Evaluation4, one restricted4EC choice (Labour Economics selected) and compulsory12EC seminar. The former three-free-choices interpretation is wrong. Choice24 and Career Skills2 remain genuine requirements; thesis10 is individual and major-linked. The old2022 thesis registration listing is an administrative record, not a current taught offering; current award structure and2026TER govern. Public2027–28preview and historical study-path/transition documents are not substituted for this current programme. Complete firsttwo years before seminar,96EC for Career Skills; Economics thesis admission follows major-seminar admission, unlike the separate Econometrics passed-seminar rule. Zero-credit mentoring/practical requirements remain separate.

alternatives.label: Economics, business & data
alternatives.labelReason: The completed UCR curriculum is broader than pure economics: it combines micro- and macroeconomics with accounting, finance, marketing, strategy, organisational study, data science, econometrics and international business.
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible response to Economics and Business Economics combining markets, macroeconomics and policy with accounting, finance, marketing, strategy, organisations, statistics, data and econometrics.
progression: Each placement is checked against current offerings, earlier formal prerequisites, four courses per term and first-year PPD. Mathematical, statistical and algorithmic foundations were also considered as advisory preferences; limited availability may place some complementary methods together.
traceOverrides: provides multivariate statistics and experimental methods that strengthen empirical economic and business research

alternatives.label: Behavioural economics, marketing & consumer decisions
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines behavioural economics with social psychology, experimental methods, marketing, persuasion, product design and data analysis, so the label reflects both the behavioural foundation and its consumer/marketing application.
alternatives.concept: A behavioural-economics and consumer-decision route combining economic choice with psychology, experiments, marketing, persuasion, product design and empirical analysis.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces Mathematical Methods, Probability & Statistics, the AI-economy course, international business and finance with social psychology, rhetoric, leadership communication, persuasive communication and negotiation. The resulting curriculum retains the common economics, business and empirical core but makes human influence, consumer response and strategic communication a distinct organising emphasis.
progression: Each placement is checked against current offerings, earlier formal prerequisites, four courses per term and first-year PPD. Mathematical, statistical and algorithmic foundations were also considered as advisory preferences; limited availability may place some complementary methods together.

alternatives.label: Finance, economics & quantitative analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around finance and economics with substantial mathematics, programming, data, econometrics and optimisation, rather than implying a specialist finance degree without a quantitative core.
alternatives.concept: A financial-economics route combining money, banking and corporate finance with micro- and macroeconomics, public economics, econometrics, probability, calculus, programming, databases, machine learning and optimisation.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces experimental methods, marketing, consumer-product work, organisational psychology and market research with programming, database systems, computational decision-making, linear algebra and advanced calculus. It therefore retains the economics and business core while making quantitative financial and economic analysis the organising emphasis. It differs still more clearly from the behavioural route, which concentrates on psychology, marketing, persuasion and consumer response.
progression: Each placement is checked against current offerings, earlier formal prerequisites, four courses per term and first-year PPD. Mathematical, statistical and algorithmic foundations were also considered as advisory preferences; limited availability may place some complementary methods together.

routeSelection.route: Economics of Markets and Organisations major
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Dutch Economics and Business Economics bachelor. The 2026–2027 programme requires one third-year major. Economics of Markets and Organisations most broadly continues the common curriculum's study of markets, firms, incentives and organisational choices rather than selecting a narrower application such as finance or marketing. The route is selected independently of UCR fit. Its seminar is fixed, while its three 4-EC course slots are approved route choices rather than three manufactured fixed courses.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match covers the programme-wide generator interests. The two remaining coherent generator-backed directions are behavioural economics with consumer/marketing decision-making and financial economics/financial markets. Both yield feasible curricula that are substantively distinct from the closest match and from each other, so the maximum of three UCR alternatives is reached.

blocks: Microeconomics & Behavior develops consumer choice,imperfect competition,strategic behaviour,general equilibrium and efficiency. It is a substantive partial relationship to the introductory microeconomics sequence.
Public Economics directly addresses the public-goods,externalities,intervention and distribution part. Personnel economics and worker incentive design remain differences.
The comparator contains a dedicated History of Economic Thought course. UCR does not add an unrelated history course merely to imitate this component.
Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations overlaps with organisation, markets and strategy but does not reproduce the comparator course in full.
Both study financial instruments and financial decisions. UCR emphasises banking,monetary institutions and risk; the comparator emphasises corporate valuation and investment/financing choices.
International Business & Governance overlaps with international economic and institutional environments but is broader and more business-governance oriented.
Research Methods & Statistics provides statistics and empirical research foundations, but is broader than Applied Statistics 1.
Linear Algebra directly covers matrix and vector methods in the comparator course, but not its full calculus, game-theory and linear-programming combination.

Ethics supplies utilitarian and other moral-theory foundations. It does not reproduce economic social-welfare functions,social-choice theory or the complete philosophical critique of welfare economics.
Personal & Professional Development overlaps with academic and professional formation but does not reproduce the comparator's economics-specific Academic Skills modules.

notes.text: Erasmus Economics and Business Economics provides a fixed two-year specialist sequence with dedicated History of Economic Thought, intermediate accounting and deeper programme-specific economics, statistics and research, followed by an approved third-year major, seminar and major-linked thesis. UCR can build coherent economics/business, behavioural-consumer and finance/quantitative programmes, but none reproduces that complete specialist sequence or the selected EUR major. In particular, no unrelated history course, invented major elective or generic UCR project is presented as the comparator's missing component.

audience.programmeDescription: Economics and Business Economics at Erasmus University Rotterdam combines a two-year specialist foundation in economics, business economics and quantitative methods with third-year choice space, Career Skills, an approved major, a major seminar and a major-linked bachelor thesis. This review fixes the Dutch full-time 2026–2027 Economics of Markets and Organisations route.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three UCR programmes offer related study through broad economics, business and data; behavioural economics, marketing and consumer decisions; or finance, economics and quantitative analysis. Each sustains economics, business and empirical study, but UCR does not reproduce Erasmus's full fixed specialist sequence, approved selected-major offer, seminar or major-linked economics thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The2026–2027 major requires Economics of Markets and Organisations,Impact Evaluation and a12EC seminar. This pathway selects Labour Economics as its4EC restricted elective. Genuine24EC choice space,Career Skills2 and a10EC major-linked individual thesis remain separate.

cellNotes.text: Econometrics provides genuine causal and predictive analysis in Stata, but it is one UCR course rather than Erasmus's dedicated statistics, econometrics and research sequence.

Accounting & Corporate Finance includes financial and management accounting,financial-statement analysis and investment appraisal. It does not reproduce the full introductory/intermediate accounting sequence.
This course examines AI's business, economic, governance and ethical implications. It supplies context, not technical data-science or econometric methods.
Statistics & Experimental Methods provides substantive multivariate methods for human research, but it is not an economics-specific research sequence.
Persuasive Communication studies framing, nudging and influence as communication practice; it complements rather than substitutes for behavioural economics.
Money, Banking & Finance provides practical financial analysis, risk and investment context; it is not Erasmus's Financial Economics major.

Decision-making in AI studies Bayesian and temporal models,expected utility,Markov decisions and multi-agent interaction. These contribute decisions under uncertainty; they are not a dedicated finance course.
PPD supports first-year academic and professional formation; it is broader than Erasmus's economics-specific Academic Skills and Career Skills components.
